purpose: Falsify the assumption that one canonical EffectGate-owned transaction is by itself sufficient for the WP105 UNKNOWN/no-blind-replay law by inspecting ambiguous post-dispatch exception classification in the currently bound EntityOS implementation.

coordination.reason: The active WP105 lane retains mutation authority. This artifact records independent negative evidence only.

observed_source_sequence: EffectGate.execute creates the canonical PENDING row with EffectJournal.begin before entityos_bridge.run.
EntityOSBridge.run crosses the execution boundary through subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout).
A timeout or other return-path exception can occur after process creation and therefore does not prove that the invoked program produced no real effect.
EffectGate.execute catches every Exception from entityos_bridge.run, writes terminal journal status FAILED through EffectJournal.complete, then re-raises.
EffectJournal has explicit UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART vocabulary, but the ordinary ambiguous post-dispatch exception path does not use an UNKNOWN terminal classification.

falsifier.claim_under_test: A single canonical EffectGate-owned transaction automatically preserves the UNKNOWN-outcome law for every ambiguous post-dispatch failure.
falsifier.counterexample: The child may have crossed the execution boundary and produced an effect before EntityOSBridge.run raises, including timeout/lost-return classes. The current generic except Exception path nevertheless finalizes the canonical effect as FAILED. FAILED is stronger than the evidence supports in this case.
falsifier.replay_risk: If downstream logic interprets canonical FAILED as definite non-application, a retry could duplicate an already-applied effect. F2 cannot safely overwrite that stronger canonical journal fact with its own UNKNOWN classification without becoming a competing outcome authority.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: Every exception from EntityOSBridge.run is guaranteed to occur before child process execution.
counterhypotheses.reason: The subprocess execution boundary is entered inside run and has an explicit timeout; the catch is outside that call and is not limited to pre-spawn exceptions.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: FAILED is intentionally equivalent to UNKNOWN and cannot drive replay.
counterhypotheses.reason: EffectJournal already carries an explicit UNKNOWN_AFTER_RESTART state, so FAILED and UNKNOWN are distinct vocabulary. No reviewed current binding defines FAILED as non-replayable uncertainty.

counterhypotheses.hypothesis: F2 can simply relabel canonical FAILED as UNKNOWN.
counterhypotheses.reason: That would create a competing outcome authority. Canonical effect authority must expose the uncertainty itself or an authority-owned receipt must make pre-dispatch vs post-dispatch failure mechanically decidable.

minimum_behavior: distinguish mechanically proven pre-dispatch failure from exception after execution may have started
persist ambiguous post-dispatch exception as explicit UNKNOWN/non-replayable or retain PENDING for canonical reconciliation
never promote ambiguous post-dispatch exception directly to a definite negative fact
reconcile canonical UNKNOWN before any retry
preserve exact effect_id, semantic request identity, generation, lease and source provenance
F2 consumes canonical uncertainty and never overwrites it
